targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(dedicated_fleet, ''), '(shared)') AS "fleet", COUNT(*) AS "hulls" FROM ships WHERE player_id=(SELECT MAX(id) FROM players) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Hulls by Dedicated Fleet

panels.description: % of standing scout posts whose WORST market age is within the post's freshness target.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE max_age <= freshness_target_seconds) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)), 0) FROM (SELECT sp.system_symbol, sp.freshness_target_seconds, MAX(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - md.last_updated))) AS max_age FROM scout_posts sp JOIN market_data md ON SPLIT_PART(md.waypoint_symbol, '-', 1) || '-' || SPLIT_PART(md.waypoint_symbol, '-', 2) = sp.system_symbol AND md.player_id = sp.player_id WHERE sp.kind = 'standing' AND sp.player_id=(SELECT MAX(id) FROM players) GROUP BY 1, 2) t

panels.title: Standing Posts Meeting Target

panels.description: THE freshness measure: market_data age per posted system vs the scout post's own target. Sorted worst-first.

targets.rawSql: SELECT sp.system_symbol AS "System", sp.kind AS "Kind", sp.hulls AS "Hulls", sp.freshness_target_seconds AS "Target (s)", COUNT(DISTINCT md.waypoint_symbol) AS "Markets", ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - md.last_updated)))) AS "Avg Age (s)", ROUND(MAX(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - md.last_updated)))) AS "Max Age (s)", CASE WHEN MAX(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - md.last_updated))) <= sp.freshness_target_seconds THEN 'FRESH' WHEN AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - md.last_updated))) <= sp.freshness_target_seconds THEN 'PARTIAL' ELSE 'STALE' END AS "Status" FROM scout_posts sp LEFT JOIN market_data md ON SPLIT_PART(md.waypoint_symbol, '-', 1) || '-' || SPLIT_PART(md.waypoint_symbol, '-', 2) = sp.system_symbol AND md.player_id = sp.player_id WHERE sp.player_id=(SELECT MAX(id) FROM players) GROUP BY sp.system_symbol, sp.kind, sp.hulls, sp.freshness_target_seconds ORDER BY MAX(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - md.last_updated))) DESC NULLS FIRST

panels.title: Fuel Spend (cr/hr) by Operation

panels.description: Jump gate fees burned per hour, trailing 6h. The window START is clamped to the first whole minute of TRAVEL_COSTS data, so this reads the TRUE rate instead of being diluted by pre-deploy hours with no data. Expect ~1.7-1.8M/hr at current fleet size; near zero means the category filter is wrong, far higher means it is double-counting FUEL_COSTS. This is pure opex and is already inside financial.json's ex-capex operating profit — it is NOT a new cost, it is a cost that was previously invisible. TRAVEL_COSTS has NO backfill (sp-shq63): it is zero for all time before the deploy and real after, so a long window shows a step change that is an artefact of INSTRUMENTATION, not of behaviour — do not read it as a cost spike.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(-SUM(amount) * 3600.0 / NULLIF(GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - GREATEST((SELECT date_trunc('minute', MIN(created_at)) + INTERVAL '1 minute' FROM transactions WHERE category='TRAVEL_COSTS'), NOW() - INTERVAL '6 hours'))), 0), 0), 0) FROM transactions WHERE category='TRAVEL_COSTS' AND created_at >= GREATEST((SELECT date_trunc('minute', MIN(created_at)) + INTERVAL '1 minute' FROM transactions WHERE category='TRAVEL_COSTS'), NOW() - INTERVAL '6 hours') AND player_id=(SELECT MAX(id) FROM players)

panels.title: Travel Spend (cr/hr)

panels.description: Gate transits per hour, trailing 6h, window clamped to the instrumented era as with Travel Spend. Expect ~270-310/hr at current fleet size. Pair with the fee distribution on the right: spend falls either by jumping less or by jumping cheaper, and this tells you which lever moved. Filtered on transaction_type='JUMP' rather than the category alone so the count stays literally correct if TRAVEL_COSTS ever widens beyond gate fees. TRAVEL_COSTS has NO backfill (sp-shq63): it is zero for all time before the deploy and real after, so a long window shows a step change that is an artefact of INSTRUMENTATION, not of behaviour — do not read it as a cost spike.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(COUNT(*) * 3600.0 / NULLIF(GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - GREATEST((SELECT date_trunc('minute', MIN(created_at)) + INTERVAL '1 minute' FROM transactions WHERE category='TRAVEL_COSTS'), NOW() - INTERVAL '6 hours'))), 0), 0), 0) FROM transactions WHERE category='TRAVEL_COSTS' AND transaction_type='JUMP' AND created_at >= GREATEST((SELECT date_trunc('minute', MIN(created_at)) + INTERVAL '1 minute' FROM transactions WHERE category='TRAVEL_COSTS'), NOW() - INTERVAL '6 hours') AND player_id=(SELECT MAX(id) FROM players)

panels.title: Jumps/hr

panels.description: Jump gate fees as a percentage of operating profit BEFORE those fees (revenue less all non-travel opex, ex-capex). Currently ~42%: routing is the single largest controllable drag on the trading business, which is what makes this a decision rather than a line item. Use it to price routing work — a change that cuts jumps 10% is worth ~4% of gross operating profit. Numerator and denominator share ONE clamped window (start = first whole minute of TRAVEL_COSTS data), which is essential: an unclamped ratio would divide minutes of fee data by hours of profit and read far too low. Expect this to be volatile for the first hour after a deploy — the denominator is lumpy over short windows because a single large cargo buy dents gross profit — and to settle as the 6h window fills. TRAVEL_COSTS has NO backfill (sp-shq63): it is zero for all time before the deploy and real after, so a long window shows a step change that is an artefact of INSTRUMENTATION, not of behaviour — do not read it as a cost spike.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(ROUND(100.0 * (-SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE category='TRAVEL_COSTS')) / NULLIF(SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE category NOT IN ('SHIP_INVESTMENTS','TRAVEL_COSTS')), 0), 1), 0) FROM transactions WHERE created_at >= GREATEST((SELECT date_trunc('minute', MIN(created_at)) + INTERVAL '1 minute' FROM transactions WHERE category='TRAVEL_COSTS'), NOW() - INTERVAL '6 hours') AND player_id=(SELECT MAX(id) FROM players)

panels.title: Jump Cost — Share of Gross Operating Profit

panels.description: Cost of a single gate transit, 15m buckets. This distribution has never been visible before and is the number that says whether routing changes pay for themselves: if p75 sits far above p50, a minority of expensive jumps carries the spend and lane selection is the lever; if the band is tight, only jumping LESS reduces cost. Currently p25/p50/p75 ≈ 5.2k/5.5k/6.4k. Unlike the stats to the left this honours the time picker directly, so it will show empty buckets before the deploy rather than a misleading flat line. TRAVEL_COSTS has NO backfill (sp-shq63): it is zero for all time before the deploy and real after, so a long window shows a step change that is an artefact of INSTRUMENTATION, not of behaviour — do not read it as a cost spike.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '15m'), percentile_cont(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY -amount) AS "p25", percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY -amount) AS "p50", percentile_cont(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY -amount) AS "p75" FROM transactions WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND category='TRAVEL_COSTS' AND transaction_type='JUMP' AND player_id=(SELECT MAX(id) FROM players) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
